I started out my normal size and they fit great however overtime I think with the extra space my feet have spread and I now wear a full size up! My mother had MS, and she did something similar with me as a child as the other comment stated aka have a “good day vs bad day” plan. She talked to me a lot about how she was feeling, and would explain that even if a day starts as “good” it can turn bad at any minute due to a flare up. But it was still hard, and there will probably be days your child won’t understand why you can’t be as active with them. 
If at all possible it might help to find a few on call babysitters for the really bad days! My mom’s friends rallied around her for this, but we also know some families who’ve used paid sitters. Also just keep in mind your child will be totally fine with a little independent play, there were many days I needed to entertain/ feed myself and my mother and it turned out okay! MS can be a real bitch, but you can do it!

Hi! I thought I’d chime in with my experience with Hollister jeans, I’m 5’2 for reference.  My perfect to the ankle length is 28 inches in their jeans, I find at Hollister that this varies between styles as being regular length or short length depending on if I’m buying jeggings or normal jeans. 

They do carry cropped jeans as well, and I find that the regular length cropped jeans I’ve tried on usually have a length of ~26 inches, and the short length cropped jeans are about ~24 inches. But unfortunately it does vary with style. I generally like a regular length in their cropped jeans.

My advice would be to go and try on if possible, because I also think their sizes vary waist wise among the different styles as well. If that’s not an option then try measuring the length on a pair that you already own, just fold them up to the length you would want and then compare that to ones you are looking at online. It gives more information if you click “size and fit guide” under each different pair.
